clue.text: Captain converted money at the border

parts.note: brass is old slang for cash
a bound is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: A ship's master changed currency at a frontier post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain converted' alludes to Shaw's play Captain Brassbound's Conversion, whose title character is the captain who is converted; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of a George Bernard Shaw play is a sea captain who undergoes a conversion.

clue.text: Oxford college in game on film

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
a skin is a thin film or layer

explanation.surface: Some Oxford college appears in a sporting movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruskin College is an institution in Oxford named after the Victorian critic.

clue.text: Troubles in a long run causing theatre closures

explanation.surface: A play's lengthy stint brings problems that shut playhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a stage show running; really a runner gets sharp side pains, and an operating theatre closes wounds with sutures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp pains in the side afflict runners, and a surgeon's sutures close wounds in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Sending off for a serious offence

definitions.text: Sending off for a serious offence

parts.words: Sending off for a serious offence
parts.note: reads like a football referee's red card, but means exile imposed as punishment for a grave crime

explanation.surface: A player is shown the red card for a nasty foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile from one's country is a penalty imposed for grave wrongdoing.

clue.text: Collapse in opening

explanation.surface: Something gives way inside a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Downfall or ruin is one sense; unfastening or loosening something is the other.

clue.text: Ivories cut very small

explanation.surface: Piano keys are chopped into tiny bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivories' suggests piano keys, but gambling cubes were once made of ivory and are called that too.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaming cubes are nicknamed ivories, and chopping food into small cubes is the cookery sense.

clue.text: Ignite to operate this

parts.note: to fire something is to set it alight
to work a machine is to operate it

explanation.surface: Light it to set it going.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrotechnic device is set off by lighting its fuse.

clue.text: Detachment shown by Government leaders in Europe

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for Europe

parts.note: Britons call mainland Europe the Continent

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here the head of Government

explanation.surface: A breakaway group led by heads of government across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The British call mainland Europe 'the Continent'; G goes inside CONTINENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A military detachment is a group of troops sent off from a larger force.

clue.text: It's fashionable now to like old colour

parts.note: what is in is currently in fashion
dig is slang for to like or appreciate

explanation.surface: A trendy person admits a fondness for a vintage shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue-violet hue sits between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Subscribed a shilling ar first as specified

indicators.note: the article and shilling come before the other word, at its start

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling
to subscribe a document is to sign it

explanation.surface: Someone put their name to a one-shilling payment exactly as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allotted or designated has been set down as stated.

clue.text: Surrounded by stuff, hothead's become too excited

indicators.note: the head letter is enclosed within the word for gorging

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to overeat
the head of hot is its letter H

explanation.surface: Gorging themselves, a hot-tempered person gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hothead' is read as the head of 'hot', H, which goes inside OVEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To get overheated figuratively is to grow too agitated or inflamed.

clue.text: Slowly move part of foot

explanation.surface: Creep along a fraction of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward gradually is one sense; a twelfth of the imperial length unit is the other.

clue.text: Trendy boy I go out with in awe

parts.note: in means fashionable
Tim is a boy's name
to date someone is to go out with them

explanation.surface: A fashionable lad takes a girl out and is overwhelmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe someone is to frighten or cow them, the verb sense of the definition.

clue.text: Something passed on when odd man out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A garment inherited when the extra person is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing given to a younger sibling after an elder outgrows it is inherited goods.

clue.text: Speaker one introduced to mother authorized delay

indicators.note: the speaker and one are put into the word for mother

parts.note: mum is mother
an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A speaker is presented to someone's mother and an official pause is approved.
explanation.definitionFit: A legally sanctioned suspension of activity or payment is an officially permitted postponement.

clue.text: Barman needing to lose a stone to become light

indicators.note: the barman must shed the stone, so the stone sits inside the light

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle
ST is the abbreviation for a stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A pub worker on a diet hopes to shed fourteen pounds to get lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the barman's word loses ST to become TAPER. A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who draws beer from the tap in a pub is an old word for a bartender.

clue.text: Navigational aid sailor put under masts

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailor is written beneath the masts

parts.note: masts are poles
tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is placed below the ship's masts to help it find its way.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern guiding star has long been used by sailors to find their bearings.

clue.text: Bend one's knee in bed

explanation.surface: Kneeling in one's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit servilely is one sense; a low wheeled bed stored under another is the other.

clue.text: Gallant royalist

explanation.surface: A brave supporter of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English Civil War the king's supporters were Cavaliers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing courtly gentleman is one sense; a supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War is the other.

clue.text: Tip reduced even in restaurant

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or tip

indicators.note: the word even is shortened by a letter, as in the poetic contraction

explanation.surface: A smaller gratuity is left even at the eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts EVEN to EEN, the poetic e'en.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria or dining room in a workplace or school.

clue.text: Whence division can supply a thin line of soldiers?

definitions.text: Whence division can supply a thin line of soldiers?

parts.words: Whence division can supply a thin line of soldiers?
parts.note: an army unit seems meant, but the diva Nellie Melba gave her name to crisp thin toast, and soldiers are strips of toast

explanation.surface: Asks which army division could send a thin line of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are British slang for fingers of toast; 'division' hides 'diva', the singer Melba.
explanation.definitionFit: Very thin crisp slices of bread are named after the Australian soprano Nellie Melba.

clue.text: Garment that's not quite a match

indicators.note: the word for match is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: a vesta is a short wooden match

explanation.surface: An outfit that doesn't quite go together.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is an old name for a match; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An undershirt, or a waistcoat in American usage, is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Second runner's a cheerful looking type

parts.note: a miler is a runner over a mile

explanation.surface: The runner-up is a happy-looking sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grins a lot looks cheerful.

clue.text: Absent-minded dunderhead is characteristic

parts.note: the head of dunder is its letter D
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person shows typical forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' is read as the head of 'dunder', D.
explanation.definitionFit: Distracted and preoccupied, someone whose mind is elsewhere.

clue.text: A bit of skirt said to attract attention

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a skirt

explanation.surface: An attractive woman is talked about to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of skirt' is slang for a woman, but here it is the hem of the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A throat-clearing sound is uttered to get someone's notice.

clue.text: Billie, eg, appears unusually fit for match

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Billie, for example, looks unexpectedly ready for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suitable for marriage, a desirable partner, is a good match.

clue.text: Suspicion about Pole's daze state

indicators.note: the word for suspicion goes around the pole

parts.note: a trace or suspicion is a slight hint
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: Doubts surround a Polish man's bewildered condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamlike, half-conscious condition is a stupor.

clue.text: In France, my term's arranged round painting in Paris area

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the word for painting
arranged means the letters of term are put in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
painting is art

explanation.surface: A French speaker's wording is set around a picture in a Parisian district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns 'term' into TMRE, which 'round' wraps about the painting word; MON is simply French for 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilltop artists' quarter of the French capital is a district of Paris.
